name: Reef 500 Index
tagline: Owns the 500 biggest fish in the sea.
beginnerDescription: One purchase gets you a slice of 500 of the largest companies in the (fictional) country.
advancedDescription: Passive large-cap index fund, market-cap weighted, 0.03% expense ratio.
newReason: A classic index fund: one basket, hundreds of companies.

name: Open Ocean Total Market
beginnerDescription: Holds big, medium and small companies all at once, so you own nearly the whole market.
advancedDescription: Passive total-market index fund covering large, mid and small caps, 0.04% expense ratio.
newReason: Even broader than Reef 500: big and small companies together.

name: Kelp Forest Bond Fund
beginnerDescription: Lends money to governments and companies that pay it back with interest. Moves less than stocks.
advancedDescription: Aggregate investment-grade bond index, intermediate duration, 0.05% expense ratio.
newReason: Bonds usually bounce around less than stocks. That's this level's lesson.

name: Tidepool Treasury Fund
beginnerDescription: Short loans to the government. Very calm, but grows slowly.
advancedDescription: Short-duration government Treasury index, low rate sensitivity, 0.03% expense ratio.
newReason: The calmest water in the game: low risk, low growth.

name: Far Waters International
beginnerDescription: Owns companies outside your home country, so you aren't relying on just one economy.
advancedDescription: Developed ex-US equity index, includes currency exposure, 0.07% expense ratio.
newReason: Your first fund outside the home market. Compare its fee to the others.

name: Deep Trench Tech
beginnerDescription: Only tech companies. Can grow fast, but can also drop hard when tech has a bad year.
advancedDescription: Concentrated single-sector fund. Higher assumed return and much higher volatility, 0.10% expense ratio.
newReason: A sector fund: all your eggs in one (tech) basket.

name: Current Rider Active Growth
tagline: A captain picks the fish for you.
beginnerDescription: A manager hand-picks stocks trying to beat the market. You pay much more for that effort.
advancedDescription: Actively managed large-cap growth fund, 0.85% expense ratio. Same assumed gross return as the index funds here.
newReason: An active fund that charges about 28x more than Reef 500. Watch the fee drag.

name: Coral Small Cap
beginnerDescription: Owns smaller companies. They can grow a lot, but their prices swing more.
advancedDescription: Passive small-cap index fund, higher volatility and size premium assumption, 0.06% expense ratio.
newReason: Smaller companies with bigger swings. Is time on your side?
